submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent: 5.98e-6 A at V0.858Zr0.142. This film is a V2O5-rich mixture with some ZrV2O7. V2O5 is stable and has the smaller predicted gap (HSE 2.83 eV), so it absorbs strongly at 3.22 eV. Photocurrent rose steeply towards the V-rich end, and index 12 beat both of its neighbours that were measured.

rejected.reason: Measured 3.73e-6 A, lower than index 12. The most V-rich film is not the optimum.
Measured 8.4e-7 A. Near phase-pure ZrV2O7 has a gap of 3.14 eV, only just below the photon energy, so it absorbs poorly.
Not measured. ZrO2-rich films have wide band gaps and would absorb little at 3.22 eV. The downward trend towards Zr also argues against them.

consultations.verdict: Support: ZrV2O7 is on the MACE hull (0 eV/atom) and MEGNet HSE gap 3.14 eV sits just below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so the phase-pure composition near V=0.667 (index 14) should absorb and be well-crystallized.

Support: V2O5 is stable (on hull) with a smaller predicted gap (2.83 eV HSE) than ZrV2O7, so the V-rich end (index 10, V=0.88; V2O5 + ZrV2O7 mixture) should absorb more of the 3.22 eV light. Testing the opposite side of the V-rich range from index 14.

Weak support: V2O5, which is the absorbing phase with the smaller gap, dominates the V-rich end. That fits the measured trend (V=0.88 gives 4x the current of V=0.67). Index 12 (V=0.858) is next to the current best and tests whether a small amount of ZrV2O7 improves the V2O5-rich film. Uninformative on the exact optimum.
